pass_a_gloss: And this also we know, that us, persuaded by Jesus to leave behind the idols and the many-god godlessness, the enemy is not able to persuade toward idol-serving, but he wants to use force; and because of this, against whom he takes authority he works such things, and either martyrs or idolaters he will make of those being tried. Many times, even now, he says: these things all I will give you, if falling you bow down to me. Let us pay attention then, lest we serve idols and put ourselves under the demons; for the idols of the nations are demons. And what sort of thing it is, having left behind the good yoke of Christ and his light load, again to put oneself under a demons' yoke and to lift a load of heaviest sin, after our having known that ash is the heart of those serving idols and more dishonoured than mud is their life, and after our having said: how false were the idols which our fathers acquired, and there is not among them one who rains.
pass_b_english: We know this too: once Jesus has persuaded us to abandon idols and the godlessness of many gods, the enemy cannot persuade us to worship idols, but he wants to force us. That is why he works such things against those over whom he gains power, and he will make those who are tested either martyrs or idolaters. Often, even now, he says, “All these things I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me” (Matthew 4:9). So let us take care that we never worship idols and subject ourselves to demons; for the idols of the nations are demons.

What a thing it is to leave Christ's kindly yoke and his “light” “burden” (Matthew 11:30), and to put oneself once more under a yoke of demons and carry a burden of the heaviest sin, after we have come to know that “the heart” of those who serve idols “is ashes” and “their life is more worthless than clay” (Wisdom of Solomon 15:10), and after we have said, “How false are the idols our fathers acquired, and there is no one among them who sends rain” (Jeremiah 16:19; 14:22)!

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 32); the old English was misaligned: this chapter's text had been attached to chapter 31, and the English given here belonged to chapter 33 (Nebuchadnezzar, Haman); this chapter is now translated in its own place, in full.
The ἄν with a present indicative has no clear force; translated 'Often, even now, he says'.

choices.issue: ὑετίζων (Koetschau, from Contra Celsum V 33; MP Delarue ὑετίζειν)
choices.choice: 'no one among them who sends rain'.
'Christ's kindly yoke'; the Greek plays on χρηστός / Χριστός, which English cannot keep (noted).
